 "Summary": "Treat the K support normals, expanded by label-preserving augmentations, as a conformal calibration set so that each test image gets a conformal p-value and the decision threshold carries a finite-sample false-positive guarantee within the modality.",

 "Rationale": "Both parents compare test scores with support-normal references (z-scores, empirical p-values) but treat the few support statistics as if they were the population, so their thresholds are noisy at small K. The obstacle is resolution (K = 4 gives p-values in steps of 1/5); label-preserving augmentations (small rotations, flips, intensity jitter) of each support create more exchangeable-like calibration views.
